title: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization
meta_description: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: Customer 360 & Hyper-Personalization: the composed architecture, the platforms underneath and the metric the program is judged on.
The problem this solution exists for
Customer truth is scattered across product silos, channels and vendors; personalization runs on segments built quarters ago, and privacy governance arrives as an afterthought that blocks launches.
Our approach

We build the identity spine first (consent-scoped, clean-room-ready), unify behavioral, transactional and service data with certified definitions, then wire decision APIs for next-best-action into every channel with measurement that proves incrementality.
Components

items: Durable IDs, consent scopes and preference management
Streaming unification with certified customer definitions
Next-best-action, offers and timing served in the moment
Profiling governance designed before the first campaign

blocks.x: Platform stack
The solution runs on Dataq Nexus and Dataq Forge: Enterprise decisions in milliseconds — with a full evidence trail for each decision. The governed data estate every AI program needs.
How it runs in an engagement

items: Baseline metrics for this problem locked with owners; current-state decision/data flow mapped in two weeks.
Gated pilot on bounded scope with the testable criterion agreed by finance before the first build sprint.
Staged rollout on the platform stack with SLOs, replay evidence and operator enablement.
Challenger models and policies quarterly; conformance monitoring; annual value audit against baseline.

blocks.x: What you get

items: Reference architecture adapted to your estate, with the integration contracts itemized.
The composed capability live on bounded scope, with audit evidence produced automatically.
Runbooks, SLO catalog and the named-pod accountability chain for production.
Baseline pack, measurement method and the quarterly review template your finance team signs.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness
Data readiness matters more than data volume: the diagnostic phase surfaces gaps, and the design phase prices them — no program pretends the estate is cleaner than it is.
Proof

items: Real-time fraud decisioning on instant rails: 38% lower fraud losses at a higher approval rate
KYC refresh backlog cleared: 70% faster cycles with agentic file assembly

blocks.x: Industry fit

Deployed across Retail & Consumer Goods, Banking & Financial Services, Telecom, Media & Entertainment, Insurance & Risk. Each industry play adjusts the regulatory frame, the integration surface and the KPI set — the pattern stays, the physics changes.
Outcomes we commit to
How a delivery runs

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.

blocks.x: What you receive
Four named artifacts are delivered in the first quarter of every program of this type:

items: The signed measurement of where the metric stands today, with the method written out so the number can be defended to finance.
Every automated decision path, its policy checks, its human checkpoint and its owner on one page.
Logs, evaluations and approvals collected automatically as the program runs — ready for internal audit or a regulator.
A running record of the delta against baseline, updated at every gate, reviewed at every steering meeting.
